title: Hang-Tenant's Exam
summary: Madame Traction is examining candidates for a Keel Town hang-tenant's licence — not with paperwork, with gates. Thread her course: off the winch base, round the dockmaster's hut, over the mesa top, and down the Keel Town hairpin before her kettle boils. The kettle is regulation.

objectives.label: Stage at the winch base — between the chalked hooks, facing downhill
The exam: dockmaster's hut → mesa top → the Keel Town hairpin, before the kettle

offer.text: Varga. I keep the Keel Ten's pilots flying honest and the examiners retired. A licence from me means the masts trust you with their ropes — but I test on gates, not paper. Paper doesn't banking-turn.

Course, and learn the shape: launch between the winch hooks, thread the dockmaster's hut without waking Vane — you won't; he audits in his sleep — crest the mesa top, and commit to the hairpin down to Keel Town's hanging boards. The kettle is the clock. When it whistles, you're firewood.
What does a courier want with a hang-tenant's licence?

Landing rights on the boards, winch priority, and the deep comfort of regulation moorage. Also — someday you'll want to land somewhere that isn't sand. I have examined the future, child. It arrives by air.

accept.text: Kettle's on. Gate one is authority — take Vane's hut tight; sloppy passes there fail pilots. Gate two is altitude — the mesa takes confidence and repays it. Gate three is the hairpin and it has ended more licences than the Guild has. Dip your nose. Trust the rope-lines. Fly.
Vane on the board. For the record, candidate: my hut post-dates the course and pre-dates your excuses. Moorings close on the whistle. If you clip my washing line, the fine is denominated in rope.

Traction's kettle exam! Kid, I passed that thing on a bike with one brake and a dream. Short-shift the mesa climb — carry speed in, not throttle — and treat the hairpin like a drift, not a turn. The boards forgive a slide. They do not forgive a straight line.

complete.text: Whistle-judged and passed. Note the kettle: still building its voice. You beat it by a mouth and a half. The Keel Ten can count on their fingers, child, and they all saw you land.

Hang-tenant Varga. The boards at Keel Town are yours to land on, the rules of moorage are yours to read — posted, seventh revision, argued hourly — and the kettle is yours to beat again any season you doubt yourself.
Then you buy the kettle a new whistle and fly again at dawn. Failure, child, is just moorage before the final approach. The Ten have a saying: *the rope is short, the sky is not.* Fly home.

choices.prompt: Traction asks what to stencil on your licence plate.

options.text: "Just my name. The landing can do the talking."
